title: The year of sorrow
hook: in one year, he loses both Khadijah and Abu Talib, his wife and his protector
carry: grief is a year, not a day

segments.voice: Yesterday, a just king in Abyssinia who wept at Surah Maryam and would not give the refugees up. Your line was a just king. Did you thank someone who protects strangers? Day ninety-three.

Some years take more than one thing from you. The same year the job goes, the parent gets sick. The same winter, two funerals. Anyone who's lived through a year like that knows: the second loss doesn't just add to the first. It lands on a bruise. For the Prophet ﷺ, about ten years after the cave, came a year like that. The Muslims had just come through a long boycott, years when Quraysh refused to trade with his whole clan or marry into it, and families went hungry in a narrow valley. It had finally ended. And then, within a short time of each other, the two people who had held him up all his life died.
screen: `SOME YEARS TAKE TWO THINGS.` → `A LONG BOYCOTT, JUST ENDED.` → `THEN, TWO DEATHS.`

segments.voice: First his uncle, Abu Talib. The man who took him in at eight, raised him, and for ten years of mounting hostility stood between his nephew and Quraysh, because in that society an attack on him meant answering to his clan. Muslims differ on Abu Talib's faith: many Sunni scholars, following a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, hold that he died without accepting Islam, while Shi'a Muslims hold that he was a believer. All remember his protection with honor. And then Khadijah. His wife of twenty-five years. The first to believe. The one who wrapped him in a blanket and said, Allah would never disgrace you. Gone. Muslims call it 'am al-huzn, the Year of Sorrow. And it didn't end with the two funerals. With Abu Talib gone, the protection was gone too, and the insults grew bolder. Ibn Ishaq tells how someone threw dirt on the Prophet's head in the street, and he went home, and one of his daughters washed it off, crying, and he told her: don't cry, my daughter, Allah will protect your father. Notice that nobody is told to hurry past this. The seerah names a whole year after grief. And years later, when the Prophet's baby son Ibrahim died, a hadith in Bukhari says he wept openly and said: the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. Tears are not a lack of faith. The Qur'an gives words for moments like this, which many Muslims say at every loss: “Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.” And from a surah of this Meccan time: “But lo! with hardship goeth ease.”
screen: `ABU TALIB, HIS PROTECTOR.` · `KHADIJAH, HIS WIFE AND FIRST BELIEVER.` · `'AM AL-HUZN: A YEAR NAMED FOR GRIEF.` · `THE EYES SHED TEARS; THE HEART GRIEVES.` · then, large: `GRIEF IS A YEAR, NOT A DAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with a loss that came in pairs. Settle, and breathe. If you've had a season when more than one thing went at once, let it come to mind, gently. You don't have to relive it. Just name both things, quietly. Notice where it sits in your body. Let it be as heavy as it is. If you haven't had a year like that, think of someone who is in one now. If you pray, you can say: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we belong to Allah, and to Him we return. The bell holds the time.
The year of sorrow. 'Am al-huzn: the year he lost both Khadijah and Abu Talib, his wife and his protector.
Your line: grief is a year, not a day. Today, check on someone who lost someone months ago, after the casseroles stopped. Tomorrow, he looks for help in another town. Day ninety-three.

howItsDone: Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un on hearing of any death or loss; mourning is marked with prayer, visits and food for the bereaved, and tears are understood as mercy, not weakness.

fork.setup: you're the Prophet's daughter. your father comes home with dirt thrown on his head in the street, months after your mother died. you wash it off, crying. what does he say?
options: don't cry, my daughter; Allah will protect your father.
fork.reveal: Ibn Ishaq reports: don't cry, my daughter, Allah will protect your father.

trapdoor: what you thought: a sad year in his life.
what it means: after years of boycott, he lost his wife and his protector together, and the seerah names a whole year for the grief.
what a scholar hears: Abu Talib's death also ended the clan protection that kept the Prophet safe in Mecca, which is why the insults and the search for help in Ta'if follow.
